newsitem.title: CHINA: Tsingtao restructuring to boost returns.
newsitem.headline: Tsingtao restructuring to boost returns.

text.p: A corporate restructuring by China's Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd is aimed at rebuilding the beer maker's stock market image and will boost returns for investors, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
Tsingtao this month created a holding company, Tsingtao Brewery Group Co, to hold the state's 44.42 percent stake in the company, which is listed in Hong Kong and Shanghai.
Creating the holding company was an attempt to rebuild Tsingtao's image in the stock markets, China Daily quoted group chairman Li Guirong as saying.
Some non-core assets and surplus workers would be stripped from the company, strengthening the listed part of the company and boosting its earnings per share, Li said.

Tsingtao has in the past come under heavy fire from overseas investors, who have accused the company of failing to live up to its promises to use proceeds from its Hong Kong share issue to expand production.
Authorities in China's eastern Qingdao city, the brewery's home base, had given their support to the restructuring, China Daily quoted company general manager Peng Zuoyi as saying.
The Qingdao government had promised to return taxes to Tsingtao, guaranteeing the company the funds it needed to reorganise, Peng said.

The new group structure would allow Tsingtao to forge into new business ventures and the company was planning to buy several beer makers in Shandong province to boost production more quickly, the newspaper quoted him as saying.
It gave no details of any tax rebates or of the brewer's expansion plans.
Tsingtao, one of China's few internationally recognised brands, produced 350,000 tonnes of beer in 1996, accounting for 2.2 percent of national production, China Daily said.
